title: Wheeltop EDS TX  Ican Graro | engineer inspection| cheap gravel combo First Look

takeaways.text: Size 54 (2× Shimano-routed) frame about 1,020 g, cut fork 528 g, seatpost 110 g, integrated bar 440 g, and about 300 g of spacers, compression plug and small parts.

Brake mounts and the bonded aluminium T47 sleeve were masked but not faced; paint had entered the bottom-bracket threads and needed a thread chaser, and a small gap under the cup showed a high spot. Bore alignment measured within about 30 microns.

Headset seats were round and clean apart from a small unsanded ridge; the seat tube interior was serviceable but not spotless. A borescope showed some splintering at a rivnut and wax or fibreglass debris near the bottom bracket, but no layer shifting.
The split-wedge headset that lets hoses pass through the bearings needs plenty of preload to clamp the steerer; split spacers ease later adjustment.
Supplied free by ICAN; listed at about US$900 for the frameset in October 2024 (about £600 delivered to the UK as the presenter recalled), with custom paint about US$1,300.
The engineer rated the finishing as budget-level and reported that ICAN said it was looking at the paint masking after he raised it.

disclosure: Hambini says in the video that ICAN sent the frame free of charge and that Wheeltop supplied the EDS groupset; the description links ICAN and a groupset store.
summary: Engineer-style inspection of a 54 cm Graro with weighed parts, thread and facing checks, bottom-bracket alignment measurement and a borescope look inside the frame and fork. Findings cover unfaced brake mounts and paint in the T47 threads, not ride quality.
